DARK WEB CREDIT CARD FRAUD

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We get an exclusive peak through the hidden doorway to an underground credit card data market on the dark web.

Unique Selling Point:
This type of credit card fraud is a growing trend & South AFricans are seemingly unaware of how vulnerable we are.
WE HACK INTO A SECURE SYSTEM TO SHOW HOW HACKERS STEAL CREDIT CARD DATA...
THEN WE GO ON TO THE DARK WEB TO SHOW THE AUCTIONS AND SALES...

EXCITING STUFF :)


Summary:
The world of a hidden data economy is one a multi-billion dollar industry.

The commercial market for personal data is booming - as the commercial value of personal data grows, cybercriminals have built an underground economy selling stolen data to anybody with a computer browser and the means to pay.

We expose a growing trend in credit card fraud and show viewers the dark web – how card details are stolen and sold.

Further information:
Further information:
Like any unregulated, efficient economy, the cybercrime ecosystem has quickly evolved to deliver many tools and services to anyone aspiring to criminal behavior. Dark Web Card Shops are sophisticated criminal enterprises covering networks of cyberthieves across the globe.
More security features on physical cards makes it harder for criminals to clone, opening the door for data based online fraud. The increase in this kind of fraud is linked to the growth of internet & mobile purchases – more people shop online.
The threat is real, and cyber-criminals constantly adapt.
THIS GOES BEYOND CARD SKIMMING

This kind of fraud is not just related to when cards are lost, skimmed or cloned. THIS IS NEXT LEVEL CREDIT CARD FRAUD! The data is accessed when there are breaches to online stores and platforms where card details are stored.

There are different levels of data for sale – costs goes up with the details linked to the card like the geographic source of the card, the CVV security code and available balances on the card can also push the price up.
SOUTH AFRICAN TRENDS
CNP or Card not Present Fraud is on the rise in South Africa– big time! From R59.5 million in 2010 to a whopping R189,2 million in 2015 in financial losses.
This fraud occurs when neither the card holder or the card is present during the illegal transation. This kind of fraud makes of 75% of SA issued credit card fraud.
But the majority of the fraud occurs outside of South Africa (60%)
USA – R33.9 million
UK – R26.6 million
FRANCE – R2.9 million
GERMANY – R2.8 million
SWEDEN – R3.3 million

SO HOW DOES THIS HAPPEN?
CREDIT CARD DATA GETS AUCTIONED AND SOLD ON THE DARK WEB TO NETWORK OF GLOBAL CYBER CRIMINALS
South African credit cards retail for between $12 and $21.
ONCE YOU GOT THE DATA – THE WORLD IS YOUR OYSTER
Once a credit card number is stolen, it can end up anywhere in the world. Some credit card thieves will simply resell the card numbers to other people on the dark net in bulk for fractions of what they can charge. Sometimes stolen credit card marketplaces become so saturated with stolen data that these card merchants will sell cards for just a few dollars. For a higher price, you can purchase stolen credit cards with specific BINs (Bank Identification Number) to increase the success rate of using the stolen card.
Once these CC numbers leave the dark net, a majority of them end up being used on online marketplaces. Charges for online subscriptions like VPNs, Netflix, Spotify, and Tidal are common because they can often go undetected.
About 1/3rd of stolen credit cards end up being used in stores, or at physical point of sale machines.
The life of a stolen credit card is a long one, potentially passing half a dozen hands before it’s used for fraud. Business and law enforcement entities lack the resources to adequately enforce smaller levels of fraud. While fraud results in higher interest rates for consumers, it’s a largely victimless crime.
THE IMPACT – WHY SHOULD YOU CARE?
Credit card fraud leads to consumers losing billions, banks losing tens of billions, and merchants losing hundreds of billions. These loses result in higher interest rates for credit card users, and a more restrictive and draconian system to loss prevention that results in the legitimate businesses and honest costumers losing money. While fraudulent charges are only a small fraction of all credit card transitions, an entire underground economy exists around the buying and selling of stolen credit cards.
THE DARK NET
The dark net, a hidden corner of the internet that’s unreachable using traditional search engines and requires the use of a specialized software.
Corporate Mentality
In a world where dishonour among thieves is the order of the day, some cyber thieves offer replacement policies if the merchandise doesn’t deliver – that way keeping their dark web cred in tact – they even rely on social validation like positive feedback from previous buyers, even responidng to customer reviews and complaints.

SOLUTIONS
Cyber Security Experts constantly mornitor global threats and are regualrly implementing new initiatives that counter cyber thieves. South African initiatives like 3D secure shopping for e-commerce merchants, the advent of CVV codes and chip cards all help combat cyber data crime, but most critical is consumer online behaviours - don’t place orders on sites that aren’t secure – and never send mails with exp & CVV numbers.

VO: New Credit card fraud trends have morphed into the global digital realm and South Africans are not immune…

VO: South Africa loses around R250 million annually to credit card fraud.

WAYNE: Financial data is the keys to your kingdom // Everything about you exists digitally

VO: John Wilson’s card was debited for R16 000. Jacqui Needham’s for 33 000. And Gemma Gardner’s for 10 and a half thousand.

All three, had their credit cards in their possession.

JACQUI: I actually got the fright of my life.
GEMMA: We have this idea that it will never happen to me – but it does happen
JOHN: It was just that transaction out of the blue. // to me it was a big mystery I don’t know how it happened

VO: This fraud is not linked to lost or stolen cards that get cloned and physically used in stores. This, is the next level – the theft is completely digital!

LINK: All the answers are right here, the number, your name, the expiry date and the CVV number on the back – and while you’re keeping it safely in you wallet, you’re leaving it all over the internet.

VO: Card Not Present fraud is where the card information is compromised says Susan Potgieter from the South African Banking Risk Information Centre or SABRIC.

SUSAN: Card not present fraud is the last crime in a chain of crimes, if the data was not compromised you will not be able to do card not present fraud. INT1 M6

VO: Globally, it’s the fasted growing trend in credit card fraud - making up 75% of all financial card losses in South Africa – coming in at a whopping 189 million Rand in just 2015.

As chip and PIN cards become more secure, it’s opened the door for data breach fraud.

SUSAN: It’s the payment platform being targeted…. Like to operate on the internet.

VO: But Jacqui Needham insists she’s cautious even with her card details online.

JACQUI: Where it says save your details – I’ve never allowed it, yes save it, always said no. // how it happens only heavens knows INT1 M8

LINK: While you may not be hacked as an individual on your devices, the websites you visited – where you’ve left your information – can be.

VO: While card skimming still exists, the digital landscape has become a hacker’s paradise, cyber security expert – Christo Boshoff, says online merchants are the biggest weak link in financial data fraud.

CHRISTO: When you go online to a bidding website or an online store – you provide your info – you’re not just entering it to the front end and it’s gone – that information is being stored in the database store that information on their system.

VO: These data breaches are peddled in a multi billion dollar hidden economy within the Internet.

Imagine the Internet is like a city, with perfectly safe areas, and then, some dodgy parts.

CHRISTO: The dark web is like 12 o’clock at night walking down a dark alley in JHB city centre – very little protection.

LINK: Getting to the dark web requires you to jump through a maze of servers – that hide your IP address, guaranteeing you anonymity.

VO: Dark Web Card Shops are sophisticated criminal enterprises, using networks of cyber-thieves across the globe, who constantly adapt their methods operating on an invisible platform.

Wayne Olsen develops cyber security solutions for the corporate world.

WAYNE: It might be double as big as the drug trade – and one thing difficult to catch these criminals – drug trade processed and moved around – this is in the digital realm and often anonymous. It’s basically the Amazon Web services of anything illegal online.

VO: Christo gave us a sneak peak into the dark web.

CHRISTO: Fraud
DEVI: Tab that says fraud…
CHRISTO: accounts and bank drops, CVV and cards, personal info, scans, weapons, drugs, software – there are CVV – 3981 entries – resellers – each having batches and batches of cards.

WAYNE: While we might think we are in the deepest darkest Africa, the fact that our info available in the digital world – we are part of this global community

VO: South African card details retail for between 12 and 21 US Dollars.

Depending on what data is available – a card with the CVV security code and expiry date will fetch a higher price.

CHRISTO: Some of your better cards where you get guaranteed limits – seller will say between 5 and 7000 US dollars on this card for $150

VO: Jacqui, John and Gemma’s cards were all used to buy international airline tickets.

JOHN: I immediately knew it was a fraudulent transaction because I didn’t book a flight

VO: Travel related purchases make up the bulk of fraudulent card not present transactions says Susan.

SUSAN: Criminals want money – they want the fasted route to money – and that is why they buy commodities for which there is a set off or a black market.

VO: About 60% of all card fraud is perpetrated outside of South Africa.

The USA tallies up just under R34 million, while the UK accounts for just over 26 million – South African cards are making it on to global underground markets through the dark web.

WAYNE: The problem is when you have bulk breaches – try and cover it up – don’t want info known – reputational damage to them.
CHRISTO: the minute the institution disclose they’ve been breached – people are notified – if not notified – that’s good for the dark the cards fetch a higher

VO: While the banks are actively trying to curb card fraud – the challenge is that they can’t win the war in isolation says Susan.

SUSAN: there is a drive from the banks to assist all the players to comply with international best practices to mitigate this crime risks.

VO: These practices have been outlined in the international Payment Card Industry Security Standards.

CHRISTO: they are trying to tell bank and merchants to keep as little info as possible – that is not globally enforced.

VO: In the meantime, for cyber-thieves – it’s a free for all.

Christo showed us just how easy it was to buy card details.

CHRISTO: Here we can now go pick what we want ST1 M14
CHRISTO: Can then go choose – visa or mastercard – we can get amex – fresh amex from the USA excellent quality – it tells you whether you can bid of it or if it’s on a fixed price – amounts vary… if you buy bulk you get discount. ST1 M8

VO: The preferred payment method is ironically not credit cards – but, the crypto currency BitCoin.

CHRISTO: It’s anonymous – if you set it up correctly and use your account correctly it’s not traceable.

VO: Catching cyber criminals is not an easy task.

SUSAN: The fact that it’s not one criminal implies – different groups of criminals in different jurisdictions // officers need to deal with the global network – makes policing this difficult.

DEVI: This is the problem – whole underground market
CHRISTO: We are trying to address the symptoms – this market place is created because of other security flaws in the system.

VO: And those flaws come at a cost to the consumer in the long run.

SUSAN: There is a financial loss – impacts on banks bottom line – can impact on the fees structure.

CHRISTO: The real problem is we are enabling them // Vicious circle – we are all complacent // we need to break the cycle.

VO: While our lives are increasingly linked to cyberspace, consumers need to
adapt their purchase patterns and become more tech savvy.

WAYNE: Don’t go and share private info unless you’re doing it with reputable organization, Don’t give credit card details away, have virus protection and don’t connect to WIFI hotspots.

SUSAN: By not being vigilant you could without intent be perpetuating the crime trend – be vigilant. We should not allow criminals to bleed us dry in SA.

PROMO 1
VO: Stolen Credit card details are traded on the dark web & South African aren’t immune.

WAYNE: it’s basically the Amazon Web services of anything illegal online.

VO: Credit Card Fraud has gone digital - cybercriminals trade compromised financial data in an underground economy – selling to highest bidder.

GEMMA: We have this idea that it will never happen to me – but it does happen

VO: The bulk of fraudulent credit card purchases – are travel related – cyberthieves are booking flights and accommodation using stolen card info.

metadata.Summary: The world of a hidden data economy is one a multi-billion dollar industry. The commercial market for personal data is booming - as the commercial value of personal data grows, cybercriminals have built an underground economy selling stolen data to anybody with a computer browser and the means to pay. We expose a growing trend in credit card fraud and show viewers the dark web – how card details are stolen and sold.
metadata.Further information: Further information: Like any unregulated, efficient economy, the cybercrime ecosystem has quickly evolved to deliver many tools and services to anyone aspiring to criminal behavior. Dark Web Card Shops are sophisticated criminal enterprises covering networks of cyberthieves across the globe. More security features on physical cards makes it harder for criminals to clone, opening the door for data based online fraud. The increase in this kind of fraud is linked to the growth of internet & mobile purchases – more people shop online. The threat is real, and cyber-criminals constantly adapt. THIS GOES BEYOND CARD SKIMMING This kind of fraud is not just related to when cards are lost, skimmed or cloned. THIS IS NEXT LEVEL CREDIT CARD FRAUD! The data is accessed when there are breaches to online stores and platforms where card details are stored. There are different levels of data for sale – costs goes up with the details linked to the card like the geographic source of the card, the CVV security code and available balances on the card can also push the price up. SOUTH AFRICAN TRENDS CNP or Card not Present Fraud is on the rise in South Africa– big time! From R59.5 million in 2010 to a whopping R189,2 million in 2015 in financial losses. This fraud occurs when neither the card holder or the card is present during the illegal transation. This kind of fraud makes of 75% of SA issued credit card fraud. But the majority of the fraud occurs outside of South Africa (60%) USA – R33.9 million UK – R26.6 million FRANCE – R2.9 million GERMANY – R2.8 million SWEDEN – R3.3 million SO HOW DOES THIS HAPPEN? CREDIT CARD DATA GETS AUCTIONED AND SOLD ON THE DARK WEB TO NETWORK OF GLOBAL CYBER CRIMINALS South African credit cards retail for between $12 and $21. ONCE YOU GOT THE DATA – THE WORLD IS YOUR OYSTER Once a credit card number is stolen, it can end up anywhere in the world. Some credit card thieves will simply resell the card numbers to other people on the dark net in bulk for fractions of what they can charge. Sometimes stolen credit card marketplaces become so saturated with stolen data that these card merchants will sell cards for just a few dollars. For a higher price, you can purchase stolen credit cards with specific BINs (Bank Identification Number) to increase the success rate of using the stolen card. Once these CC numbers leave the dark net, a majority of them end up being used on online marketplaces. Charges for online subscriptions like VPNs, Netflix, Spotify, and Tidal are common because they can often go undetected. About 1/3rd of stolen credit cards end up being used in stores, or at physical point of sale machines. The life of a stolen credit card is a long one, potentially passing half a dozen hands before it’s used for fraud. Business and law enforcement entities lack the resources to adequately enforce smaller levels of fraud. While fraud results in higher interest rates for consumers, it’s a largely victimless crime. THE IMPACT – WHY SHOULD YOU CARE? Credit card fraud leads to consumers losing billions, banks losing tens of billions, and merchants losing hundreds of billions. These loses result in higher interest rates for credit card users, and a more restrictive and draconian system to loss prevention that results in the legitimate businesses and honest costumers losing money. While fraudulent charges are only a small fraction of all credit card transitions, an entire underground economy exists around the buying and selling of stolen credit cards. THE DARK NET The dark net, a hidden corner of the internet that’s unreachable using traditional search engines and requires the use of a specialized software. Corporate Mentality In a world where dishonour among thieves is the order of the day, some cyber thieves offer replacement policies if the merchandise doesn’t deliver – that way keeping their dark web cred in tact – they even rely on social validation like positive feedback from previous buyers, even responidng to customer reviews and complaints. SOLUTIONS Cyber Security Experts constantly mornitor global threats and are regualrly implementing new initiatives that counter cyber thieves. South African initiatives like 3D secure shopping for e-commerce merchants, the advent of CVV codes and chip cards all help combat cyber data crime, but most critical is consumer online behaviours - don’t place orders on sites that aren’t secure – and never send mails with exp & CVV numbers.
